title: AI code passes security checks 56% of the time
sources: Veracode 2026 GenAI Code Security Report (press release): average security pass rate 56% across 100+ models, virtually unchanged since the 2025 report; syntax pass ~100%; coding-specific and larger models showed little security advantage
OWASP Top 10 (secrets, injection, access control) for the checklist

lines.text: AI code runs *almost every time.* | It passes *security* checks | only *56 percent* of the time.
First, that's from *Veracode's 2026* report, | testing *over a hundred* AI models | on the same coding tasks.
Second, the code *compiled* nearly always. | So *it runs* | isn't the same as *it's safe.*
Third, *bigger* models weren't safer. | And models built *for coding* | did no better.
And finally, that score barely moved in a *year,* | while the models got *smarter* at everything else.
So before you ship AI code, | check where your *secrets* live, | what *user input* can do, | and *who* is allowed in.
Reading the code you ship is the real skill now. | Go to teyro dot app, | or search *Teyro.*
